title: api: standardize rate-limit semantics, idempotency keys, and Retry-After for OpenAI compatibility
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers integrating via the OpenAI-compatible surface observed inconsistent rate limit headers, ambiguous Retry-After values, and missing guidance for idempotent request semantics when using streaming and function/tool-calling endpoints. This PR unifies rate-limit response headers across the Redwood API and OpenAI-compat layer, adds explicit idempotency key handling for creation endpoints, and provides deterministic Retry-After semantics for both short-term throttling and longer backoff windows. Summary of changes: - Add X-RateLimit-* headers and ensure they are present on 429 responses for all text/generation, chat/streaming, and function-calling routes. - Standardize Retry-After to be returned as a single integer (seconds) and as an RFC-1123 Date in Retry-After-Date for human-readable cases; prefer seconds for machine clients. - Implement idempotency-key validation & deduplication for non-idempotent operations (create completion, tool invocation session start). Keys are honored for 24h by default with configurable TTL per customer. - Streaming stability: when an idempotent request is replayed during a streaming session we now return an immediate 409 with a machine-readable error body referencing the original request id unless the original run completed successfully, in which case we return the cached result. - Consistent error codes: introduce a small error-code catalog (RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, IDMP_KEY_CONFLICT, IDMP_KEY_EXPIRED, STREAM_RESUMPTION_FAILED) surfaced in the JSON body under "error.code" for both native and OpenAI-compat responses. - API compatibility: OpenAI-compat layer maps Redwood headers to the OpenAI expected fields while preserving the canonical Retry-After semantics. Backwards compatibility: existing clients that ignore the new headers are unaffected; those using idempotency keys will see dedup semantics. Security: idempotency keys are validated for length, entropy, and rate of creation per project to mitigate abuse. Testing/QA: added unit tests, integration tests that simulate burst throttling and replayed idempotent requests, and a perf canary for streaming under throttle. Checklist: [x] Update API surface and docs [x] Unit tests [x] Integration tests covering streaming + idempotency [x] Load test for rate-limit semantics [x] OpenAI-compat mapping verification Related: ENG-5124 maps to the backend orchestration tickets that enable TTL storage for idempotency entries. Deployment notes: feature gated behind runtime flag api.idempotency.enabled and rollout is staged (5% -> 25% -> 100%) to prevent mass cache effects. Rollback plan: flip the feature flag; a hotfix endpoint to flush idempotency cache per-customer is available.

release_notes: Standardize rate-limit headers and Retry-After semantics; add idempotency key support for generation and tool-invocation endpoints; introduce consistent error codes for rate-limit and idempotency-related failures. Backwards-compatible and feature-gated.
notes: Staged rollout over two weeks. Monitor metrics: rate_limit_429_count, idempotency_cache_hit, streaming_resume_errors. If 429s spike unexpectedly after rollout, rollback flag api.idempotency.enabled and reduce rollout percentage.
